# Scenix v1.6.0 — Shader Nodes And Node Materials

Scenix `1.6.0` adds the optional `scenix-nodes` crate: typed shader graphs,
node materials, and a post-node effect language with WGSL and GLSL ES 3.00
backends. Node materials are a first-class renderer draw path, the post stack
executes generated effects, and the browser preflight compiles graphs to GLSL
before anything is uploaded. Every v1.6 surface is additive and behind the
`nodes` feature; the default facade build behaves exactly like v1.5.0.

## Highlights

- `scenix-nodes` is a standalone, `no_std`-capable CPU crate: build a
  `ShaderGraph`, validate it, and mutate CPU state with zero GPU involvement.
- Graphs carry three output ports: `fragment_color`, `fragment_alpha`, and an
  optional vertex `vertex_offset` displacement port. Only the live subgraph is
  validated and lowered; dead nodes are released by construction.
- A typed `ShaderNodeKind` vocabulary covers uniforms, vertex attributes,
  world/view fragment sources, texture sampling, splat/component shaping,
  arithmetic, `Mix`/`Clamp`/`Smoothstep`, the five-slot `Remap`, `Fresnel`,
  sRGB/linear conversion, four lighting styles, tone mappers, and fog. Nodes
  carry stage metadata, so fragment-only or post-only nodes in another stage
  produce specific `NodeDiagnostic`s instead of broken shaders.
- The WGSL backend emits modules that match the renderer bind contract exactly:
  group 0 frame, group 1 object, group 2 material (uniform + sampler +
  texture_2d), group 3 set up for fragment-stage lights, and six varyings that
  mirror the built-in vertex layout. `Time` compiles to the frame elapsed slot.
- Codegen deduplicates common subexpressions, prunes dead nodes, and treats
  vec3 lighting/fog results correctly (alpha rides the `vec4` constructor
  because WGSL forbids implicit `vec3` → `vec4` casts).
- `NodeMaterial` pairs a graph with CPU state (base color, emissive, metallic,
  roughness, alpha mode/cutoff, double-sided, texture id). It reports the
  `FEATURE_NODE_GRAPH` bit, a `Custom` shader-kind pipeline key, a stable graph
  hash that ignores live CPU state, and optional `serde` support.
- `Renderer::register_node_material` (behind the renderer's `nodes` feature)
  registers slots, packs node uniforms in the standard material block, builds
  node pipelines lazily per `NodeMaterialSlot`, switches pipelines per draw,
  buckets transparency from the slot's alpha mode, and rejects unregistered
  node materials during culling with the same error pipeline as built-ins.
- `PostNodeEffect` post graphs ship atomic presets (passthrough, vignette,
  desaturate, posterize, pixelate, color grade, exposure) plus
  `scenix-post::NodeEffectProgram`, which owns one generated module, builds
  per-format pipelines lazily, and drives the `[f32; 8]` parameter contract
  through the standard post pass.
- The `scenix-wasm` browser preflight compiles a serialized `NodeMaterial`
  into GLSL with a diagnostic payload (`compile_node_material_glsl`) or
  validates it without codegen (`validate_node_material_json`) — no GPU, no
  renderer state, panic-free JsValue surfaces.
- Color-like nodes (lighting, tone mapping, fog, conversions) accept rgba base
  colors directly and drop alpha in codegen, so scripts authored against vec4
  colors flow through unchanged.

## Small Example

```rust
use scenix::{
    generate_material_wgsl, LightingStyle, Material, NodeInput, NodeMaterial, ShaderGraph,
    ShaderNodeKind, UniformInput, WgslOptions,
};

// Base color pulses over time, then feeds a Lambert lighting term.
let mut graph = ShaderGraph::new();
let base = graph.push(ShaderNodeKind::Uniform(UniformInput::BaseColor));
let time = graph.push(ShaderNodeKind::Uniform(UniformInput::Time));
let pulse = graph.add(
    ShaderNodeKind::Multiply,
    vec![NodeInput::Node(base), NodeInput::Node(time)],
);
let lit = graph.chain(ShaderNodeKind::Lighting(LightingStyle::Lambert), pulse);
graph.add_fragment_output(lit, None);

let material = NodeMaterial::new("pulse", graph);
assert!(material.validate().is_empty());
assert!(material.feature_bits() & scenix::FEATURE_NODE_GRAPH != 0);

let wgsl = generate_material_wgsl(&material, &WgslOptions::default()).unwrap();
// wgsl.source() is renderer-ready: bind groups 0..=3 follow the scenix
// contract, and Time resolved to frame.resolution.z.
```

## Feature Flags

- `nodes`: enables `scenix-nodes` through the facade with curated re-exports
  (node vocabulary, materials, generators, diagnostics, parameter slots).
- `nodes` + `renderer`: node-material slots enter the draw path with lazy
  pipelines and per-draw `set_pipeline` switching.
- `nodes` + `post`: `NodeEffectProgram` executes generated post graphs.
- `nodes` + `wasm`: browser-side GLSL preflight for node editors.
- `scenix-nodes` standalone: `no_std`-capable CPU crate (std/serde features).

## Examples

```sh
cargo run -p scenix --example nodes_material --features nodes
cargo run -p scenix --example nodes_wgsl --features nodes
cargo run -p scenix --example node_post_effect --features nodes
```

## Compatibility

- All 18 workspace crates are version `1.6.0` and require Rust `1.89`.
- No existing enum gained variants; default features are unchanged.
- The renderer frame uniform now packs `[width, height, elapsed, 1 / height]`;
  built-in shaders are unaffected, and direct `FrameUniform` consumers outside
  scenix should account for the elapsed slot.
- Node graphs that cannot resolve produce a typed `NodeDiagnostic`
  (`StageUnsupported`, port mismatches, cycles, `UnknownNode`) rather than a
  panicking pipeline; `NodeMaterial::validate` covers the fragment stage and
  `ShaderGraph::validate(Stage::Vertex)` covers displacement ports explicitly.
- GPU-gated tests (`SCENIX_RUN_GPU_TESTS=1`) cover headless node rendering,
  mixed node/builtin draws, culling rejection, and registration validation;
  dedicated benchmarks cover graph build/lower hot paths.

See the [full changelog](../../CHANGELOG.md) and the
[node API guide](../../docs/api/scenix-nodes.md) for API and verification
details.
